tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Free start times for a service between two instants (at most 14 days). A time that has started, or that starts within the business's minimum notice, is not offered.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Ask for a price on something custom. Creates a quote_request item.

tools.description: Request a service at a time. Check availability first. endTime and reservationFor.name may be left out: they follow from the service (its length, its name). tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Order products. Prices are in minor units. A line naming a product (productId or sku) costs the business's price from list_products, and the total follows; a different price you send is only noted for the business. A line naming no product waits for the business to price it. A priced order binds you

tools.name: get_item_status
tools.description: The current state of an item you created, in the business's words: what it proposed and waits for your person to answer (offer, with its terms_sha), who it waits on, what they can do next, and the conversation so far (thread: the business's replies and your person's messages).

tools.name: accept_offer
tools.description: Accept another time the business proposed for a booking, its quote, its changes to an order, or a change it asks for to a confirmed booking or an accepted order (offer.kind change: the promise moves). This binds your person, so send terms_sha — offer.terms_sha from get_item_status — only after they

tools.name: decline_offer
tools.description: Say no to another time or to changes the business proposed (the booking request or the order is closed) or to its quote. To a change it asks for to a confirmed booking or an accepted order, no keeps what was agreed; on a change your person asked for (requested_change), it takes that back. Add reason

tools.name: suggest_time
tools.description: Instead of the time the business proposed, ask for another: start_time must be one of the free times check_availability lists (the end follows the service's length). The business confirms it or proposes again. On a confirmed booking it asks the business to move it (the end keeps the booking's length

tools.name: make_offer
tools.description: Answer what the business proposed with only what your person would change: another start_time (a booking: one of the free times check_availability lists; a quote request: the time it is for), other quantities for the lines of changes it suggested to an order (by index in offer.terms.lines; 0 drops o

tools.name: provide_details
tools.description: Answer what the business asked about an item (get_item_status says it needs a detail). The item moves on; on any other item your details are kept as a message for the business.

tools.name: withdraw_from_contract
tools.description: Your person withdraws from their booking (one they paid for) or order, within the period the business states (withdrawal on get_item_status). Two steps: without confirm_withdrawal nothing is sent and you get the statement to show them (confirm.statement); send confirm_withdrawal: true on their yes.

tools.name: request_return
tools.description: Once an order's goods reached your person: ask to send them back. reason faulty, not_as_described or wrong_item (the legal guarantee: it costs them nothing), or changed_mind (a withdrawal while a period to withdraw runs, agreed at once; otherwise a return the business answers under its own policy).

tools.name: cancel_item
tools.description: Cancel an item you created. After the business's cancellation window, a confirmed booking is cancelled late where the business records late cancellations (it may count against the customer), and refused where it does not. A confirmed stay answers first with the fee under its policy and what is owed

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Start a conversation, or reply on an item you own.

tools.name: acknowledge_receipt
tools.description: Counter-sign a receipt this item earned, so both sides hold it: a promise, a change both sides agreed to it (kind amended), how it ended, or a refund's. Read the item to find its receipts; then send a compact JWS signed with your own Ed25519 key — header {alg:'EdDSA', typ:'sdi-receipt-ack+jws', jwk:

tools.name: verify_customer
tools.description: When a result says identity.recognised is weak, the person gave the email of a customer the business knows. Call this with item_id and access_token to email them six digits; ask the person for the code and call it again with code. Then the business recognises them.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_business_profile, get_item_status, withdraw_from_contract · Private data: cancel_item · Public sink: list_services, create_booking, create_order, accept_offer, withdraw_from_contract, request_return, cancel_item, send_message, acknowledge_receipt, verify_customer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_business_profile, get_item_status, withdraw_from_contract · Private data: cancel_item · Public sink: list_services, create_booking, create_order, accept_offer, withdraw_from_contract, request_return, cancel_item, send_message, acknowledge_receipt, verify_customer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_products" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
